passages.text: Now Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchijah heard that Jeremiah had been telling all the people: “This is what the LORD says: Whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine and plague, but whoever surrenders to the Chaldeans will live; he will retain his life like a spoil of war, and he will live.
passages.sermon:
Shephatiah was the son of Mattan.
Gedaliah was the son of Pashhur.
Jucal was the son of Shelemiah.
Pashhur was the son of Malchijah.
These four men heard Jeremiah.
Jeremiah was speaking to all the people.
Jeremiah said, “This is what the LORD says.
Anyone who stays in this city will die.
They will die by the sword.
They will die by famine.
They will die by plague.
Anyone who goes out to the Chaldeans will live.
He will keep his life as a prize.
He will live.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע שְׁפַטְיָ֣ה בֶן־ מַתָּ֗ן וּגְדַלְיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־ פַּשְׁח֔וּר וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן־ שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן־ מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה אֶ֨ת־ הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־ כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ס כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ הַיֹּשֵׁב֙ בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את יָמ֕וּת בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר וְהַיֹּצֵ֤א אֶל־ הַכַּשְׂדִּים֙ יִחְיֶה וְהָיְתָה־ לּ֥וֹ נַפְשׁ֛וֹ לְשָׁלָ֖ל וָחָֽי׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: This city will surely be delivered into the hands of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD gave a message about this city.
The LORD said the city will be handed over.
The army of the king of Babylon will receive the city.
The king of Babylon will capture the city.
passages.original: כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הִנָּתֹ֨ן תִּנָּתֵ֜ן הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֗את בְּיַ֛ד חֵ֥יל מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֖ל וּלְכָדָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then the officials said to the king, “This man ought to die, for he is discouraging the warriors who remain in this city, as well as all the people, by speaking such words to them; this man is not seeking the well-being of these people, but their ruin.”
passages.sermon:
The officials spoke to King Zedekiah.
They said, “This man must die.
He is Jeremiah the prophet.
He weakens the hands of the soldiers who remain in this city.
He also weakens the hands of all the people.
He does this by speaking these words to them.
This man does not seek the peace of these people.
He seeks their harm.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ הַשָּׂרִ֜ים אֶל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ י֣וּמַת נָא֮ אֶת־ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּה֒ כִּֽי־ עַל־ כֵּ֡ן הֽוּא־ מְרַפֵּ֡א אֶת־ יְדֵי֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמִּלְחָמָ֜ה הַֽנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים׀ בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֗את וְאֵת֙ יְדֵ֣י כָל־ הָעָ֔ם לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֣י׀ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֗ה אֵינֶ֨נּוּ דֹרֵ֧שׁ לְשָׁל֛וֹם לָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה כִּ֥י אִם־ לְרָעָֽה׃

passages.text: “Here he is,” replied King Zedekiah. “He is in your hands, since the king can do nothing to stop you.”
passages.sermon:
King Zedekiah was the ruler of Judah.
The officials spoke to King Zedekiah about Jeremiah.
King Zedekiah answered the officials.
He said, “Jeremiah is in your hands.”
He said, “I cannot stop you.”
He said, “The king has no power against you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ הִנֵּה־ ה֖וּא בְּיֶדְכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ אֵ֣ין הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יוּכַ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: So they took Jeremiah and dropped him into the cistern of Malchiah, the king’s son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah with ropes into the cistern, which had no water but only mud, and Jeremiah sank down into the mud.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet in Jerusalem.
The officials took Jeremiah.
They brought Jeremiah to a cistern.
The cistern belonged to Malchiah.
Malchiah was the son of the king.
The cistern was in the courtyard of the guard.
The officials lowered Jeremiah into the cistern with ropes.
There was no water in the cistern.
There was only mud in the cistern.
Jeremiah sank into the mud.
passages.original: וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֨כוּ אֹת֜וֹ אֶל־ הַבּ֣וֹר׀ מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּח֥וּ אֶֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּחֲבָלִ֑ים וּבַבּ֤וֹר אֵֽין־ מַ֙יִם֙ כִּ֣י אִם־ טִ֔יט וַיִּטְבַּ֥ע יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּטִּֽיט׃ס

passages.text: Now Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court official in the royal palace, heard that Jeremiah had been put into the cistern. While the king was sitting at the Gate of Benjamin, Ebed-melech went out from the king’s palace and said to the king, “My lord the king, these men have acted wickedly in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have dropped him into the cistern, where he will starve to death, for there is no more bread in the city.”
passages.sermon:
Ebed-melech was a Cushite.
He was a court official in the royal palace.
Ebed-melech heard that men had put Jeremiah into the cistern.
At that time, the king was sitting at the Gate of Benjamin.
Ebed-melech left the king’s palace.
He went to the king.
He spoke to the king.
He said, “My lord the king, these men have acted wickedly against Jeremiah the prophet.
They have dropped Jeremiah into the cistern.
He will die there from hunger.
There is no more bread in the city.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֡ע עֶֽבֶד־ מֶ֨לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֜י אִ֣ישׁ סָרִ֗יס וְהוּא֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי־ נָתְנ֥וּ אֶֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ אֶל־ הַבּ֑וֹר וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּשַׁ֥עַר בִּנְיָמִֽן׃ וַיֵּצֵ֥א עֶֽבֶד־ מֶ֖לֶךְ מִבֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹֽר׃ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הֵרֵ֜עוּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ לְיִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ הִשְׁלִ֖יכוּ אֶל־ הַבּ֑וֹר וַיָּ֤מָת תַּחְתָּיו֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָֽרָעָ֔ב כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין הַלֶּ֛חֶם ע֖וֹד בָּעִֽיר׃

passages.text: So the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, “Take thirty men from here with you and pull Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies.”
passages.sermon:
King Zedekiah was the ruler of Judah.
Ebed-melech was a Cushite and a servant in the king’s palace.
King Zedekiah gave a command to Ebed-melech.
He said, “Take thirty men from here with you.”
He said, “Pull Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern.”
He said, “Do this before Jeremiah dies.”
passages.original: וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֛ת עֶֽבֶד־ מֶ֥לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר קַ֣ח בְּיָדְךָ֤ מִזֶּה֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְֽהַעֲלִ֜יתָ אֶֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֧הוּ הַנָּבִ֛יא מִן־ הַבּ֖וֹר בְּטֶ֥רֶם יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: Then Ebed-melech took the men with him and went to the king’s palace, to a place below the storehouse. From there he took old rags and worn-out clothes and lowered them with ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.
passages.sermon:
Ebed-melech was a Cushite and a court official in the royal palace.
Ebed-melech took the men with him.
He went to the king’s palace.
He went to a place below the storehouse.
He took old rags from there.
He also took worn-out clothes from there.
He tied the rags and clothes to ropes.
He lowered the rags and clothes with ropes to Jeremiah.
Jeremiah was in the cistern.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח׀ עֶֽבֶד־ מֶ֨לֶךְ אֶת־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֜ים בְּיָד֗וֹ וַיָּבֹ֤א בֵית־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ תַּ֣חַת הָאוֹצָ֔ר וַיִּקַּ֤ח מִשָּׁם֙ בְּלוֹיֵ֣ הַסְּחָבוֹת וּבְלוֹיֵ֖ מְלָחִ֑ים וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֧ם אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ אֶל־ הַבּ֖וֹר בַּחֲבָלִֽים׃

passages.text: Ebed-melech the Cushite cried out to Jeremiah, “Put these worn-out rags and clothes under your arms to pad the ropes.” Jeremiah did so, and they pulled him up with the ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
passages.sermon:
Ebed-melech was a Cushite and a servant of the king.
Ebed-melech spoke to Jeremiah.
Ebed-melech said, “Put these old rags and worn-out clothes under your arms.
Place them under the ropes.”
Jeremiah obeyed Ebed-melech.
The men pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes.
They lifted Jeremiah out of the cistern.
Jeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר עֶבֶד־ מֶ֨לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֜י אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ שִׂ֣ים נָ֠א בְּלוֹאֵ֨י הַסְּחָב֤וֹת וְהַמְּלָחִים֙ תַּ֚חַת אַצִּל֣וֹת יָדֶ֔יךָ מִתַּ֖חַת לַחֲבָלִ֑ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ כֵּֽן׃ וַיִּמְשְׁכ֤וּ אֶֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֙הוּ֙ בַּֽחֲבָלִ֔ים וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ מִן־ הַבּ֑וֹר וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ בַּחֲצַ֖ר הַמַּטָּרָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and received him at the third entrance to the house of the LORD. “I am going to ask you something,” said the king to Jeremiah. “Do not hide anything from me.”
passages.sermon:
King Zedekiah was the ruler of Judah.
Jeremiah was a prophet of the LORD.
King Zedekiah sent his servants to bring Jeremiah the prophet to him.
They brought Jeremiah to the king.
They met at the third entrance of the house of the LORD.
King Zedekiah spoke to Jeremiah.
He said, “I am going to ask you something.”
He said, “Do not hide anything from me.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֗הוּ וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶֽת־ יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַנָּבִיא֙ אֵלָ֔יו אֶל־ מָבוֹא֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ שֹׁאֵ֨ל אֲנִ֤י אֹֽתְךָ֙ דָּבָ֔ר אַל־ תְּכַחֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נִּי דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: “If I tell you,” Jeremiah replied, “you will surely put me to death. And even if I give you advice, you will not listen to me.”
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet of God.
King Zedekiah spoke to Jeremiah.
Jeremiah answered King Zedekiah.
Jeremiah said, “If I tell you the truth, you will kill me.
If I give you advice, you will not listen to me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־ צִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ כִּ֚י אַגִּ֣יד לְךָ֔ הֲל֖וֹא הָמֵ֣ת תְּמִיתֵ֑נִי וְכִי֙ אִיעָ֣צְךָ֔ לֹ֥א תִשְׁמַ֖ע אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: But King Zedekiah swore secretly to Jeremiah, “As surely as the LORD lives, who has given us this life, I will not kill you, nor will I deliver you into the hands of these men who are seeking your life.”
passages.sermon:
King Zedekiah spoke to Jeremiah in secret.
King Zedekiah made a promise to Jeremiah.
King Zedekiah said, “As surely as the LORD lives, who gave us this life, I make this oath.
I will not kill you.
I will not hand you over to these men.
These men are seeking your life.”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֞ע הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֛הוּ אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר חַי־ יְהוָ֞ה את אֲשֶׁר֩ עָשָׂה־ לָ֨נוּ אֶת־ הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ הַזֹּאת֙ אִם־ אֲמִיתֶ֔ךָ וְאִם־ אֶתֶּנְךָ֗ בְּיַד֙ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר מְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת־ נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃ס

passages.text: Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, “This is what the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘If you indeed surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, then you will live, this city will not be burned down, and you and your household will survive.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah spoke to Zedekiah.
Jeremiah was a prophet.
Zedekiah was the king of Judah.
Jeremiah said, “This is what the LORD says.”
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said, “If you surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, you will live.”
The city will not be burned with fire.
You will live.
Your household will live.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ אֶל־ צִדְקִיָּ֡הוּ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אִם־ יָצֹ֨א תֵצֵ֜א אֶל־ שָׂרֵ֤י מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶל֙ וְחָיְתָ֣ה נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ וְהָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את לֹ֥א תִשָּׂרֵ֖ף בָּאֵ֑שׁ וְחָיִ֖תָה אַתָּ֥ה וּבֵיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But if you do not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, then this city will be delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans. They will burn it down, and you yourself will not escape their grasp.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah spoke to King Zedekiah.
Jeremiah was a prophet of the LORD God of Israel.
Jeremiah gave a message from God.
He said, “If you do not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, something will happen.
This city will be given into the hands of the Chaldeans.
The Chaldeans are the Babylonians.
They will burn the city with fire.
You will not escape from their power.
You will not get away from them.”
passages.original: וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא־ תֵצֵ֗א אֶל־ שָׂרֵי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וְנִתְּנָ֞ה הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ בְּיַ֣ד הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וּשְׂרָפ֖וּהָ בָּאֵ֑שׁ וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹֽא־ תִמָּלֵ֥ט מִיָּדָֽם׃ס

passages.text: But King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “I am afraid of the Jews who have deserted to the Chaldeans, for the Chaldeans may deliver me into their hands to abuse me.”
passages.sermon:
King Zedekiah spoke to Jeremiah.
Zedekiah was the king of Judah.
He said, "I am afraid."
He feared the Jews who had deserted to the Chaldeans.
He thought the Chaldeans might give him into the hands of those Jews.
He feared those Jews would abuse him.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ אֲנִ֧י דֹאֵ֣ג אֶת־ הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽפְלוּ֙ אֶל־ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים פֶּֽן־ יִתְּנ֥וּ אֹתִ֛י בְּיָדָ֖ם וְהִתְעַלְּלוּ־ בִֽי׃פ

passages.text: “They will not hand you over,” Jeremiah replied. “Obey the voice of the LORD in what I am telling you, that it may go well with you and you may live.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah spoke to King Zedekiah.
Jeremiah said, “They will not hand you over.”
Jeremiah told Zedekiah to obey the voice of the LORD.
Jeremiah said, “Listen to what I am telling you from the LORD.”
If you obey, it will go well with you.
If you obey, you will live.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֹ֣א יִתֵּ֑נוּ שְֽׁמַֽע־ נָ֣א׀ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֗ה לַאֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ דֹּבֵ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְיִ֥יטַב לְךָ֖ וּתְחִ֥י נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: But if you refuse to surrender, this is the word that the LORD has shown me: All the women who remain in the palace of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon, and those women will say: ‘They misled you and overcame you— those trusted friends of yours. Your feet sank into the mire, and they deserted you.’
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah spoke to King Zedekiah.
Jeremiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Jeremiah said, “If you refuse to surrender, listen to this.”
The LORD has shown me what will happen.
All the women who remain in the palace of the king of Judah will be brought out.
The officials of the king of Babylon will take these women.
These women will speak to you.
They will say, ‘Your trusted friends misled you.
They overcame you.
Your feet sank into the mud.
Your friends deserted you.’
passages.original: וְאִם־ מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לָצֵ֑את זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִרְאַ֖נִי יְהוָֽה׃ וְהִנֵּ֣ה כָל־ הַנָּשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִשְׁאֲרוּ֙ בְּבֵ֣ית מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֔ה מוּצָא֕וֹת אֶל־ שָׂרֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל וְהֵ֣נָּה אֹמְר֗וֹת הִסִּית֜וּךָ וְיָכְל֤וּ לְךָ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י שְׁלֹמֶ֔ךָ הָטְבְּע֥וּ בַבֹּ֛ץ רַגְלֶ֖ךָ נָסֹ֥גוּ אָחֽוֹר׃

passages.text: All your wives and children will be brought out to the Chaldeans. And you yourself will not escape their grasp, for you will be seized by the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned down.”
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah spoke to King Zedekiah of Judah.
Jeremiah said, “All your wives will be taken out to the Chaldeans.
All your children will also be taken out to the Chaldeans.
You will not escape from the Chaldeans.
The king of Babylon will capture you.
The king of Babylon will seize you with his own hand.
The city of Jerusalem will be burned with fire.”
passages.original: וְאֶת־ כָּל־ נָשֶׁ֣יךָ וְאֶת־ בָּנֶ֗יךָ מֽוֹצִאִים֙ אֶל־ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹא־ תִמָּלֵ֣ט מִיָּדָ֑ם כִּ֣י בְיַ֤ד מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶל֙ תִּתָּפֵ֔שׂ וְאֶת־ הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את תִּשְׂרֹ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃פ

passages.text: Then Zedekiah warned Jeremiah, “Do not let anyone know about this conversation, or you will die.
passages.sermon:
King Zedekiah spoke to Jeremiah.
Zedekiah warned Jeremiah.
He said, “Do not let anyone know about this conversation.
If anyone finds out, you will die.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ אִ֛ישׁ אַל־ יֵדַ֥ע בַּדְּבָֽרִים־ הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְלֹ֥א תָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: If the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come and demand of you, ‘Tell us what you said to the king and what he said to you; do not hide it from us, or we will kill you,’ then tell them, ‘I was presenting to the king my petition that he not return me to the house of Jonathan to die there.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The officials may hear that I spoke with you.
They may come to you.
They may say to you, “Tell us what you said to the king.”
They may say, “Do not hide it from us, or we will kill you.”
They may say, “What did the king say to you?”
You must answer them.
Say, “I was presenting my request to the king.”
Say, “I asked the king not to send me back to the house of Jonathan.”
Say, “I did not want to die there.”
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִשְׁמְע֣וּ הַשָּׂרִים֮ כִּֽי־ דִבַּ֣רְתִּי אִתָּךְ֒ וּבָ֣אוּ אֵלֶ֣יךָ וְֽאָמְר֪וּ אֵלֶ֟יךָ הַגִּֽידָה־ נָּ֨א לָ֜נוּ מַה־ דִּבַּ֧רְתָּ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אַל־ תְּכַחֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נּוּ וְלֹ֣א נְמִיתֶ֑ךָ וּמַה־ דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם מַפִּיל־ אֲנִ֥י תְחִנָּתִ֖י לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ לְבִלְתִּ֧י הֲשִׁיבֵ֛נִי בֵּ֥ית יְהוֹנָתָ֖ן לָמ֥וּת שָֽׁם׃פ

passages.text: When all the officials came to Jeremiah and questioned him, he relayed to them the exact words the king had commanded him to say. So they said no more to him, for no one had overheard the conversation.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah was a prophet in Jerusalem.
The king of Judah was Zedekiah.
The officials came to Jeremiah.
The officials questioned Jeremiah.
Jeremiah answered the officials.
Jeremiah told them everything the king had commanded him to say.
No one else had heard the conversation between Jeremiah and the king.
The officials did not question Jeremiah further.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ כָל־ הַשָּׂרִ֤ים אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֙הוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁאֲל֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ וַיַּגֵּ֤ד לָהֶם֙ כְּכָל־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּחֲרִ֣שׁוּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ כִּ֥י לֹֽא־ נִשְׁמַ֖ע הַדָּבָֽר׃פ

passages.text: And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured.
passages.sermon: Jeremiah was a prophet in Judah.\r\nJeremiah stayed in the courtyard of the guard.\r\nHe remained there until the day Jerusalem was captured.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יִרְמְיָ֙הוּ֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה עַד־ י֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ נִלְכְּדָ֣ה יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑םס וְהָיָ֕ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נִלְכְּדָ֖ה יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ
